history.content: When comparing taxes on earned income versus investment income, a significant difference becomes evident. Most extremely wealthy individuals generate most of their income through investments. In many countries, income received from dividends is taxed as regular income, while profits from the sale of shares are classified as capital gains. If you have already surpassed your tax-free income limit for the year but have not exceeded your capital gains tax allowance, it might be more advantageous to realize a profit from trading rather than receiving investment income. The taxation on capital gains and other forms of investment income is where a substantial portion of wealth is concentrated. For instance, a CEO might earn around $200,000 in salary each year but have stock options worth hundreds of millions. In this case, a higher income tax has little impact on the CEO.
What is an income tax bracket?

The tax bracket is the threshold at which you begin to pay for the "services" the government provides. It's not a voluntary membership. Tax brackets refer to the range of taxable income in which you fall. An income tax bracket typically pertains to federal or state tax rather than the combined rate. Your tax bracket is determined by your total taxable income for a given year.
How the tax brackets are calculated?
Sorry, but I do not know.
How much of our income do we contribute to Social Security?
In the United States, the Social Security tax is 6.2% of the first $118,500 of your pay.
FICA, or the Federal Insurance Contributions Act, includes two types of taxes: Social Security and Medicare.
Do foreigners who work in the USA have to pay FICA taxes?

Foreigners who are not tax residents in the USA, particularly students, are not required to pay FICA taxes. However, if their home country has a social security reciprocity agreement with the United States, they may receive a credit for any FICA taxes paid when they return to their home country. For instance, a student on an F1 visa working under the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program is exempt from FICA taxes. However, once they switch to an H1B visa, they lose this exemption and become subject to FICA taxes.

Almost everyone who works in the U.S. is required to pay Social Security and Medicare taxes, commonly known as payroll taxes or FICA. However, college students employed by their college are exempt from FICA taxes (Social Security and Medicare). While you are still subject to federal and state income taxes, if you are a part-time employee earning a small amount of money, you likely will earn less by the end of the year to trigger tax withholding.
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. If you have any more questions, feel free to ask.
Are investment earnings subject to FICA taxes?

No. Investment earnings are not subject to FICA taxes. Social Security and Medicare taxes are applied to income earned from wages. If you earn a salary and pay FICA taxes, additional distributions, such as withdrawals from a 401(k)—regardless of whether they're taken early—are not subject to FICA or Medicare taxes. This is because the 401(k) funds have already been taxed at the time of contribution.
